clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive skeletal ciliopathy characterised by a markedly constricted, narrow thorax with short horizontal ribs, short limbs and, in most subtypes, polydactyly; it lies at the lethal end of the short-rib thoracic dysplasia spectrum that also includes Jeune asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy and Ellis-van Creveld syndrome.

Classically divided into overlapping subtypes: Saldino-Noonan (type I), Majewski (type II), Verma-Naumoff (type III) and Beemer-Langer (type IV), though molecular data show these are a continuum rather than discrete disorders.

Caused by biallelic variants in genes encoding intraflagellar transport and ciliary proteins (for example DYNC2H1, IFT80, WDR34, WDR60, IFT140, IFT172, NEK1, WDR35, and others), disrupting the primary cilium and Hedgehog signalling.
Polydactyly is usually pre-axial or post-axial and may involve hands and feet; Majewski type is distinguished by disproportionately short, ovoid tibiae and prominent oral/facial clefting.

Extraskeletal anomalies are common and help subtype the disorder: congenital heart defects, renal cystic dysplasia, hepatic ductal plate malformation, gastrointestinal atresia, ambiguous or anomalous genitalia and cerebral malformations.
The severe thoracic constriction produces pulmonary hypoplasia, and the condition is typically perinatally lethal from respiratory failure; diagnosis is often made antenatally or at birth.

Antenatal ultrasound may show a narrow thorax, short long bones, polydactyly and associated visceral anomalies; distinguishing it antenatally from milder short-rib thoracic dysplasia guides counselling.
It belongs to the broader family of skeletal ciliopathies, so overlap with cranioectodermal dysplasia, Sensenbrenner and Jeune syndromes reflects shared ciliary gene pathways and allelism.
reference.pathophysiology: Short-rib polydactyly syndrome is a skeletal ciliopathy arising from biallelic loss-of-function or hypomorphic variants in genes encoding components of the primary cilium, particularly the intraflagellar transport (IFT) machinery and the cytoplasmic dynein-2 retrograde motor. Genes implicated include DYNC2H1, WDR34, WDR60, IFT80, IFT140, IFT172, WDR35, NEK1 and related ciliary transcripts, several of which are allelic with milder disorders such as Jeune asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy and cranioectodermal dysplasia. The primary cilium is an essential organelle for transducing Hedgehog signalling, which governs endochondral bone growth, patterning of the limb bud and the anterior-posterior axis of the digits. When IFT-mediated protein trafficking along the ciliary axoneme fails, chondrocyte proliferation and the orderly progression through the growth plate are disrupted, producing the profoundly shortened ribs and long bones. Aberrant Hedgehog signalling also perturbs digit specification, giving rise to polydactyly, while ciliary dysfunction in the developing kidney, liver, heart and gut explains the cystic renal dysplasia, ductal plate malformation, cardiac defects and visceral anomalies that accompany the skeletal phenotype. The severity gradient across subtypes reflects the degree of residual ciliary function conferred by particular allele combinations.
additionalDifferentials: Jeune asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy (short-rib thoracic dysplasia without or with polydactyly, milder and often survivable)
Ellis-van Creveld syndrome (chondroectodermal dysplasia with post-axial polydactyly and cardiac defects)
Thanatophoric dysplasia (lethal short-limbed dysplasia with narrow thorax but no polydactyly)
Cranioectodermal dysplasia (Sensenbrenner syndrome) within the same ciliopathy spectrum
Chondrodysplasia punctata and other lethal neonatal skeletal dysplasias
Oral-facial-digital syndromes (particularly overlap with Majewski type facial clefting and lingual anomalies)
Hydrolethalus syndrome and Meckel-Gruber syndrome (other lethal ciliopathies with polydactyly and visceral malformation)
additionalInvestigations: Detailed antenatal ultrasound assessing thoracic circumference, long-bone length, digit number and visceral anatomy
Postnatal full skeletal radiographic survey documenting rib length and morphology, metaphyseal spurs and long-bone shape
Molecular genetic testing via a skeletal ciliopathy or skeletal dysplasia gene panel, or exome/genome sequencing
Fetal or postnatal echocardiography to characterise congenital heart disease
Renal and hepatic imaging for cystic dysplasia and ductal plate malformation
Perinatal autopsy with photographs and histology of bone, kidney and liver where consent is given
Genetic counselling with confirmation of parental carrier status for recurrence-risk estimation
redFlags: Severe respiratory distress at birth from pulmonary hypoplasia secondary to the constricted thorax
Antenatal detection of a markedly narrow chest with short ribs, prompting urgent multidisciplinary counselling
Coexisting major cardiac or renal malformation compounding perinatal instability
Hydrops or polyhydramnios suggesting associated visceral or cardiac compromise
Progressive hypoxaemia unresponsive to ventilatory support, indicating a non-survivable thoracic volume
reference.prognosis: The classic subtypes are almost always perinatally lethal owing to pulmonary hypoplasia from the severely constricted thorax, with most affected infants dying before or shortly after birth. Rare milder, allelic presentations that overlap with survivable short-rib thoracic dysplasia carry a better but still guarded outlook dependent on thoracic volume and visceral involvement.
pitfalls: Regarding the historical Saldino-Noonan, Majewski, Verma-Naumoff and Beemer-Langer subtypes as rigid entities rather than a molecular continuum overlapping with Jeune and Ellis-van Creveld syndromes
Assuming polydactyly is always present, since some short-rib thoracic dysplasias in the same spectrum lack extra digits
Attributing perinatal death solely to the skeletal findings and overlooking a lethal cardiac or renal anomaly
Failing to arrange molecular confirmation and carrier testing, leaving recurrence risk uncounselled for future pregnancies
Confusing it antenatally with thanatophoric dysplasia, which shares a narrow thorax but lacks polydactyly and has a different molecular basis
